answer: Let every new identity enter only through a single narrow jetty during a short tide window, one at a time, by completing a slow sequence of useful verification jobs that cannot run in parallel. Each job output feeds the next, so cloning accounts buys no speed. A mesa-shaped reputation follows: after the slow climb the identity reaches a flat plateau and may vouch for others, but its deposit stays locked and is slashed if a vouched identity is shown to share its operator. Cloning thus costs a full climb and a separate deposit each time.
